title: Regional tenancy entities and CRUD patterns
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic control-plane data model and a set of CRUD API patterns for handling resources, environments, regions, and clusters across multi-region Redwood deployments. It focuses on operational clarity: identity, replication, routing policy attachment, and safe lifecycle transitions that integrate with rollout and capacity controls.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform engineers, serving-runtime owners, and infra SREs.
- Scope: resource/entity model (IDs, ownership), environment/region/cluster relationships, routing policy model, and concrete REST-style CRUD patterns. Not a line-by-line proto; this is a design-runbook to inform API contracts and migration scripts.

Glossary (short):
- Resource: logical deployable (model, pipeline, route, policy) managed in control plane.
- Environment: logical separation (dev/staging/prod).
- Region: cloud region where clusters run (e.g., us-west1, eu-central1).
- Cluster: a pool of compute (GPU fleet) within a region; may be shared or tenant-dedicated.
- Allocation: binding of a Resource to one or more Clusters/Regions with capacity hints.
- Routing policy: rules that decide where a request is sent (latency/cost/priority/capacity).

Key principles:
1) Canonical identity: every entity has a globally unique stable id (uuid) and a human-friendly name. Name collisions are allowed per-namespace but not id collisions.
2) Single source of truth (SSoT) for control metadata: the control plane stores canonical resource state; region-local replicas are eventual and read-optimized.
3) Idempotent, versioned writes: use optimistic concurrency (version or etag) for updates.
4) Explicit bindings: resource -> environment -> allocation(s). No implicit region assumptions.
5) Minimal blocking: create operations should avoid cross-region coordination where possible; use async hooks for replication and validation.

Data model (entities and minimal fields):
- Resource:
  - id: uuid
  - name: string (unique per environment + kind)
  - kind: [model, endpoint, policy, variant]
  - owner_team: string
  - environment_id: uuid
  - default_routing_policy_id: uuid (optional)
  - created_at, updated_at, version
  - metadata: free-form map (string) -- store as stringified JSON in docs

- Environment:
  - id, name (dev/staging/prod), tenant_id (optional), account_id, created_at, updated_at

- Region:
  - id, code (us-west1), status (active/draining), properties (latency-tier, cost-tier)

- Cluster:
  - id, region_id, cluster_type (shared, dedicated), capacity_score, labels, status

- Allocation:
  - id, resource_id, region_id, cluster_id (optional), desired_replicas, min_replicas, max_replicas, traffic_weight, health_status, last_sync

- RoutingPolicy:
  - id, name, type (latency|cost|priority|capacity|explicit), rules (stringified expression), fallback_policy_id, created_by

Relationships and invariants:
- Resource.environment_id must reference an Environment.
- Allocation.resource_id -> Resource. One resource can have multiple allocations (multi-region).
- Cluster.region_id -> Region. An allocation references region and optionally specific cluster.
- RoutingPolicy may be shared across resources; policies are first-class and versioned.

Multi-region replication model (control plane):
- Global control plane (primary) holds SSoT. Region replicas cache a subset required for local routing decisions.
- Writes: all create/update/delete operations go to SSoT. If API endpoint is region-local, we forward write to SSoT asynchronously but return an operation id to caller.
- Read paths: prefer local replica for latency; fall back to SSoT for strongly consistent reads with explicit version param.
- Conflict resolution: optimistic concurrency via version/etag. For out-of-order replicate events, last-write-wins only when originating_version > applied_version; otherwise flag for manual reconciliation.

Routing policy model (conceptual):
- Policies are tree-like: a policy can reference child policies as fallback.
- Common primitives: prefer_region(list), avoid_region(list), prefer_cluster_labels(k=v), capacity_threshold(min_tokens_per_sec), cost_budget(max_cents_per_token), sticky_session(ttl)
- Policy evaluation order: 1) explicit binding (resource-level override), 2) per-environment default, 3) global default.

CRUD API patterns (REST-style endpoints and semantics):
- Base patterns:
  - POST /v1/{env}/resources -> create resource. Return 202 with operation id if async replication required.
  - GET /v1/{env}/resources/{resource_id} -> returns resource with allocations and policy ids. Query param ?consistency=strong to read from SSoT.
  - PATCH /v1/{env}/resources/{resource_id} -> partial update, requires if-match: "<version>" header for optimistic concurrency.
  - DELETE /v1/{env}/resources/{resource_id} -> soft-delete: mark tombstone and initiate regional teardown. Hard delete requires clearance and GC window.

- Allocation lifecycle APIs (key for multi-region ops):
  - POST /v1/{env}/resources/{id}/allocations -> add a new region/cluster target. Must validate region and cluster exist and are active. Returns allocation id and a validation token.
  - PUT /v1/{env}/resources/{id}/allocations/{alloc_id}/scale -> adjust replicas/weights. Require version header.
  - POST /v1/{env}/resources/{id}/allocations/{alloc_id}/drain -> mark draining (drain gracefully).
  - DELETE /v1/{env}/resources/{id}/allocations/{alloc_id} -> remove allocation; operation is async if there are active connections.

Idempotency and retries:
- All POSTs that create entities accept optional client-supplied idempotency_key. Server stores key -> created_id mapping for 24 hours (configurable).
- Clients should retry on 5xx with exponential backoff. 409 indicates version conflict.

Validation and consistency checks:
- Synchronous validations: identity, environment/region/cluster existence, basic schema.
- Async validations: capacity quotas, billing checks, cross-account routing approval. Attach validation state to allocation (pending/validated/failed).

Example flow: create a resource and bind to two regions
1) Client: POST /v1/prod/resources { name: 'gpt-cache-v1', kind: 'model', default_routing_policy: 'regional-priority' } -> 201 id=r1.
2) Client: POST /v1/prod/resources/r1/allocations { region: us-west1, desired_replicas: 10 } -> 202 alloc=a1 (status pending).
3) Async validator checks capacity in us-west1 and policy constraints; updates alloc.status -> validated and triggers region-provisioning job.
4) Client: POST /v1/prod/resources/r1/allocations { region: eu-central1, desired_replicas: 6 } -> 202 alloc=a2.
5) After both allocations are healthy, routing controller updates weights and the resource begins serving multi-region traffic.

Rollouts and canaries:
- Rollout is a change to Resource or Allocation that should not impact 100% traffic. Pattern: create new variant resource (resource.v2) or new allocation with traffic_weight small, then increase weight.
- Provide APIs for automated canary policies: POST /v1/{env}/rollouts -> define steps (percent, duration, metrics), controller executes and rolls forward/rolls back based on metric thresholds.

Access control and audit:
- All entities track created_by, updated_by, and have audit-log entries.
- RBAC: operations scoped by team and environment. Sensitive ops (delete, hard-delete, change-fallback) require elevated role.

Failure modes and operational guidance:
- Replication lag: reads with consistency=eventual may see stale allocations for a short window; clients should tolerate 30s-2m depending on region topology.
- Region drain: when a region is draining, mark region.status=draining and forbid new allocations; orchestrate traffic redistribution via routing policies.
- Partial failures on delete: tombstones stop new traffic; GC service removes metadata after retention window (default 30 days).

Migration notes (from earlier flat models):
- Existing monolithic resource model should be migrated to explicit allocations. Migration path: convert existing resource -> create allocations for each region where it is currently running, set traffic_weight to previous traffic distribution, then flip default routing to use allocations.
- Provide migration tool: read current state, propose allocations, apply with dry-run and audit log.

Monitoring and dashboards (ideas):
- Per-resource replication lag, allocation health, policy evaluation latency, per-region capacity headroom, recent version conflicts.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Should control plane allow writes at region-local endpoints that become SSoT in that region? (Tradeoff: lower write latency vs more complex reconciliation.) Current recommendation: single SSoT with regional write-forwarding.
- Conflict resolution for concurrent allocation changes originating in different regions: use version + operation origin tag and force manual reconciliation for cross-account conflicting changes.

Next steps / actionable items:
- Proto: draft OpenAPI for the described endpoints and share with serving-runtime and SRE. (Owner: Lina)
- Migration tool: PoC script to convert existing resources to allocation-first model (Owner: Marco).
- Dashboard dashboard: create Grafana panels for replication lag and allocation health (Owner: Samir).

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-PLT-1872 (control plane replication notes)
- JIRA-PLT-4951 (migration epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/914

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive — aim for APIs that are easy for SDKs and infra automation to use.
- Feedback requested: edge cases for constrained multi-tenant clusters, preferred semantics for immediate vs eventual deletes, and any expected integrations with billing/quotas that would alter validation flow.

(End of note)
